main_text.p: [illegible, ~8 letters] &c. capitibus ultimis. Attexta familiari, & epistolari clausulâ, de quâ in antecessum fusius Cap. III.

V. Usitatiorem fuisse hanc sanctissimo Apostolo methodum, haud prolixè demonstrandum. Ut nempe præmissis fidei dogmatis, munitis iis & illustratis, subjungat vitæ, morúmque præcepta. Illustre suppeditat exemplum, quæ habetur ad Romanos, iisdem omninò partibus distincta. Similiter illa ad Ephesios, quinetiam ad Galatas & Colossenses. Didacticis & dogmaticis, [illegible, ~6 letters] & moralia perpetuò attexuntur. Quando Canonicæ reliquæ Jacobi, Petri, Johannis, in genere parænetico[?], & hortatorio ferè consistunt. Vel promiscuè theoretica practicis, moralia doctrinalibus permiscent. De quo analytici Commentarores. Quanquam Pauli methodum, ad imitationem trahere potuisse alios, quis forte excipiat. page.notes: The Greek words in the first line and the Greek word after "Didacticis & dogmaticis," are damaged and could not be read; they are left as illegible. The running head is set in heavy black type with damaged letters, so "Autore" is doubtful. The word "parænetico" ends in a letter that may be Greek omicron rather than Latin o. The page number "222" is also heavily worn. The catchword "genere" sits at the lower right below the text.
